Spain coach Luis de la Fuente has confirmed that Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal is available and will join the national team squad for Sunday’s UEFA Nations League match against England. According to football transfer expert, Fabrizio Romano on X on Friday, de la Fuente was quoted as saying, “He’s available and he’s joining us today, adding that the teenager is feeling well and eager to link up with the group. Yamal missed Thursday’s 2-0 victory over Czechia in Prague after experiencing minor discomfort and inflammation in his right knee, which developed during Barcelona’s recent La Liga win over Atlético Madrid. Medical checks showed some fluid in the joint. Rather than risk the trip to Prague, de la Fuente and the medical staff decided it was better for Yamal to remain in Barcelona for treatment and recovery. The coach stressed the issue was not serious and that Yamal could have played against Czechia if necessary, but prioritising his fitness for the England game was the sensible choice. Palmer desperate to play for England – Rogers Nations League: Kane scores as England beat Croatia 2-1 to reach q’finals Spain beat Czech Republic 2-0 to retain perfect Nations League record Yamal is expected to train with the squad ahead of the match at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal, who was also absent from the Czechia game, is set to rejoin at a similar time. Spain head into the fixture as group leaders with a perfect record and an extended unbeaten run. Both teams have already secured qualification for the Nations League quarter-finals, so Sunday’s encounter will decide first place in the group. Yamal’s return provides a significant boost for de la Fuente’s side as they prepare for one of the biggest fixtures of the international window.
